featured_reviews.review_text: The owner and his son are so arrogant and rude that you will be appalled. You will be insulted left, right and centre. featured_reviews.name: Sachin Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: This Book Point shop is by far the worst I've ever encountered. The owner is not only rude but also incredibly slow; I was next in line to pick up my kid books, and it took over 30 minutes! It seems like the owner enjoys arguing about every little thing rather than focusing on running his business. I made my payment through a QR code with a RuPay credit card, only to be told later that I had to pay extra because I used a credit card. I chose not to argue because I figured my time was better spent elsewhere than giving him ammunition for another argument, which seems to be his favorite pastime. I did mention to him that it would have been better if he had informed me of this beforehand or at least disabled the credit card payment option. Charging customers for bank processing fees is not just unethical—it's a complete offense. But I’ve learned that arguing with fools only leads to frustration. featured_reviews.name: Naveed Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text: The Book Shop in Vile Parle East has been a quiet constant in my life for as long as I can remember. I’ve been visiting it since childhood, hand in hand with my father, when a good book and a peaceful afternoon felt like the perfect reward. Today, I walk those same paths with my wife, hoping that one day my child will do the same. There’s something timeless about this place—an old-world charm that refuses to fade. Books spill out onto the pavement, from classics and self-help to academic treasures, many of them second-hand and priced at a fraction of their worth. I’ve never walked away empty-handed; somehow, I always find a title that speaks to me. The affordability is a gift, especially when so much around us keeps getting more expensive. That said, I’ve heard whispers—and felt a hint myself—of the staff being a little curt or unwelcoming at times. It doesn’t happen often, but it’s there. Still, the connection I have with this shop runs deeper than a few words exchanged across a counter. It’s where stories begin—on paper and in life. And for that, I’ll always return.
